articles.title: From Pax Silica to Japan: Mapping India's AI Partnerships in 2026
articles.description: The first major global engagement in 2026 came in February, when India joined the Pax Silica initiative, a multilateral framework focussed on AI and semiconductor cooperation. As part of the initiative, India also signed the India–US AI Opportunity Partnership. The declaration outlines cooperation on trusted AI ecosystems, resilient semiconductor supply chains, digital infrastructure, and emerging technologies, while promoting collaboration on AI development and innovation among participating countries.

articles.title: Goldman Sachs top economist agrees that millions of Americans will lose jobs to AI; but rejects the idea that these will be permanently wiped out; says these CEOs are ignoring that ...
articles.description: Goldman Sachs economist Joseph Briggs forecasts AI could displace 9% of the US workforce, around 15 million jobs, drawing parallels to past tech disruptions. While acknowledging job losses in sectors like tech and consulting, he emphasizes history shows technology creates more new roles than it destroys. MIT's Neil Thompson suggests AI adoption will be gradual, with partial automation being more common than outright job elimination.
